title: Moving away from Agile: What's Next – Martin Harrysson & Natasha Maniar, McKinsey & Company
talk_summary: McKinsey consultants argue that AI coding tools yield only 5-15% enterprise gains because bottlenecks moved to work allocation, manual review, and unchanged roles/ceremonies. They propose AI-native operating models: spec-driven work, smaller consolidated pods, agent-assisted sprint planning and acceptance criteria, and outcome-based measurement.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of prose stories with fuzzy acceptance criteria, teams co-create multiple prototypes and iterate acceptance criteria with agents (security, observability) before coding, so agents get precise specs and downstream rework drops.

takeaways.technique: Route work by task type to different operating models
takeaways.what_they_do: They match operating model to task: legacy modernization = agent factory with human spec+final review; greenfield features = iterative human-agent co-creation loop. Not one model for all work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an example operating model could look like a factory of agents where humans provide an initial spec and final review with minimal intervention

takeaways.technique: Squad split by workflow (bug-fix vs greenfield)
takeaways.what_they_do: Reorganized squads by workflow type — one for small bug fixes, one for greenfield — so agents and humans specialize and context switching drops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The squads were also reorganized by workflow, so there would be one which would be focused on small bug fixes and another focused on greenfield development.
takeaways.numbers: 51% increase in code mergers cited for the bank intervention

takeaways.technique: Agent pre-computes cross-repo impact before review
takeaways.what_they_do: Background agents analyze potential cross-repository impacts so developers don't spend debugging time discovering them, and reviewers get impact context up front.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents would be used to look and impact look at the potential cross-repository impacts to prevent debugging time for developers

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a measurement stack from inputs (tool spend, upskilling time) through outputs (velocity, quality, resiliency proxies like MTTR) to economic outcomes, and warn that bottom performers measured neither speed nor productivity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building a robust measurement system that prioritizes outcomes and not just adoption is important not just to monitor progress, but also pinpoint issues
takeaways.numbers: only 10% were measuring productivity among bottom performers

takeaways.technique: Consolidated one-pizza pods with orchestrator roles
takeaways.what_they_do: Shrink teams to 3-5 consolidated 'product builder' roles that orchestrate agents with full-stack fluency, instead of separate QA/frontend/backend specialists; more pods at same headcount.
takeaways.evidence_quote: moving away from the two-pizza structure to one-pizza pods of three to five individuals
takeaways.numbers: 5-6x increase in time to market claimed for top performers
